title: What If You Never Slept Again? Day by Day

scenes.text: What if you never slept again? The first night is the easy part.
scenes.keywords: tired man staring at ceiling night

scenes.text: After one day awake, your judgment and coordination drop to roughly the level of being drunk.
After two days, natural killer cells, which fight viruses and tumors, fall by 37 percent, and hallucinations can begin.
By day three, your brain forces microsleeps of up to 30 seconds, and you often don't notice them.
The longest documented attempt was 264 hours, eleven days. Afterward, the student slept 14 hours and was medically healthy.
But rats kept from sleep died within two to three weeks, and scientists still can't say exactly why.

description:
